newsitem.title: UK: Britain bans tobacco sports sponsorship.
newsitem.headline: Britain bans tobacco sports sponsorship.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government announced Monday that it was banning sponsorship of sporting events by tobacco companies, dealing a blow to many of the nation's favourite fixtures.
Anti-smoking campaigners welcomed the move but tobacco companies said they were disappointed by a decision they said would not bring a drop in tobacco consumption.
Cigarette companies spend millions sponsoring sports such as cricket, golf, darts, rugby, show-jumping and Formula One motor racing.
But Health Secretary Frank Dobson said the sports promoters would have to learn to live without tobacco advertising and sponsorship.
"We recognise that some sports are heavily dependent on tobacco sponsorship," he said in a speech to the Congress of the Royal College of Nursing.
"We do not wish to harm these sports. We will therefore give them time and help to reduce their dependency on tobacco and replace it with sponsorship from more benign sources."

The government, which trounced the Conservatives in the May 1 election, confirmed last week that it planned to outlaw tobacco advertising, but made no mention at the time of extending the ban to sports sponsorship.
Dobson said sports authorities had to recognise that by helping to promote the sales of tobacco they were harming the health of many fans.
"The fact is that the tobacco industry, unique amongst all industries, kills around 120,000 of its own customers every year," Dobson said.
He was backed by one of Britain's main cancer charities, the Imperial Cancer Research Fund.
Spokeswoman Margaret Swain said, "We would welcome any moves that the government make to ban tobacco advertising and sponsorship."
The Tobacco Manufacturers' Association said a variety of sports would suffer financially as a result of the ban.
The group's executive director of industry affairs John Carlisle said, "We think that banning sport sponsorship will have no effect on the consumption of tobacco products.
"What it will do is make life extremely difficult for several sports who so heavily rely on tobacco sponsorship."
